note: Chapter XVII looking-in shots (Ian, 16 Nov): the house and landscape from outside, the scene through a lit window.
style: An atmospheric oil painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, the architecture and landscape outside a house with the scene glimpsed through a lit window, rich dusk and night colour. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Looking in from the street at night through the tall lit window of a grand London hotel, 1893: inside, two men stand talking in a warm sitting-room; outside, wet pavement, a gas lamp and a waiting cab. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in from the asylum garden at dusk through a tall study window, 1893: inside, a lamp-lit room where a doctor and a young dark-haired woman stand by a phonograph; outside, the old brick wall of the house, ivy, a lawn and elms against a fading sky. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in from the garden at dusk through the study window of the asylum, 1893: inside, a man bends over an open drawer of wax cylinders under a green-shaded lamp; outside, wet leaves on the sill, the brick wall and the evening sky. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in at evening from the lawn at an upstairs window of the asylum, 1893: a young woman sits alone beside a phonograph in a small lamp-lit sitting-room; the long dark front of the building, chimneys, and an autumn sky. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in from the dark garden at night through the study window of the asylum, 1893: a young woman typing and a man beside her at a desk in a pool of lamplight; the rest of the house black, rain on the glass, bare trees and a pale moon above. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

The long front of the asylum at night seen from across the lawn, 1893: one upstairs window lit gold where two small figures sit typing; the rest of the house dark, the moon over the roofs, the black trees of Carfax beyond the wall. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in at night through a barred window of the asylum, 1893: a man sits placidly on a narrow bed in a bare lit cell; outside, the rough stone wall, a drainpipe, and the dark shape of the neighbouring house Carfax among trees. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in from the garden on a grey afternoon through the tall windows of the asylum drawing-room, 1893: inside, by the fire, a tall man in black mourning has turned away and covered his face, a young woman watches him, another man lays a hand on his shoulder; outside, damp lawn and dripping elms. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.

Looking in from outside at sunset along the row of tall corridor windows of the asylum, 1893: in one window a lean man in a travelling coat stands looking out, a young woman coming towards him; red-gold sunset reflected on the glass, the brick wall and ivy. The figures inside are small, seen through the glass, with no detail in their faces; the building, garden and sky fill most of the picture.
